def shutdown_order(p):
    """
    You must terminate n running processes, one at a time, until none remain.

    p is an n x n matrix (a list of n lists of n ints) with 1 <= n <= 13,
    0 <= p[j][i] <= 10**6, and p[i][i] == 0 for every i. When process i is
    terminated, every process j that is still running at that moment (i.e.
    not yet terminated, j != i) adds an interference penalty of p[j][i].
    The total penalty of a termination order is the sum of these penalties
    over all n termination steps.

    Return a tuple (best, order) where best is the minimum achievable total
    penalty (an int) and order is a termination order achieving it, given
    as the list of process indices 0..n-1 in the order they are terminated.
    If several orders achieve the minimum penalty, return the
    lexicographically smallest such order (orders compared as lists of
    ints).

    Edge cases: for n == 1 the answer is (0, [0]); if all penalties are 0
    the answer is (0, [0, 1, ..., n-1]).

    Note the bound n <= 13: trying all n! orders is far too slow, but the
    state space of subsets of processes is small.

    >>> shutdown_order([[0, 5], [3, 0]])
    (3, [0, 1])
    >>> shutdown_order([[0, 4], [4, 0]])
    (4, [0, 1])
    >>> shutdown_order([[0, 1, 6], [2, 0, 3], [4, 5, 0]])
    (9, [0, 2, 1])
    """
